{{short description|American mathematician|bot=PearBOT 5}}
[[File:Catlin david.jpg|thumb|{{center|David Catlin, Oberwolfach 2004}}]]
'''David William Catlin''' (born 12 May 1952 [[Rochester, Pennsylvania]]) is an American mathematician who works on the theory of [[several complex variables]].

Catlin received in 1978 his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] under [[Joseph Kohn]] with thesis ''Boundary Behavior of Holomorphic Functions on Weakly Pseudoconvex Domains''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=16463}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Boundary Behavior of Holomorphic Functions on Weakly Pseudoconvex Domains|journal=J. Differential Geom.|volume=15|year=1981|pages=605–625}}</ref> He is a professor at [[Purdue University]].

He solved a boundary behavior problem of complex analysis in several variables, on which his teacher Kohn worked in detail and which was originally formulated by [[Donald C. Spencer|Donald Spencer]], a particular case of the [[Neumann problem]] for <math>\overline{\partial}</math>, a non-elliptic boundary value problem.<ref>Makhlouf Derridj, [http://www.numdam.org/article/SB_1994-1995__37__7_0.pdf La sous-ellipticité pour le problème <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann dans un domaine pseudoconvexe de <math>\mathrm{\mathbf{C}^n}</math>, d'après D. Catlin], Séminaire Bourbaki 790, 1994/95,</ref><ref>[http://www.math.unipd.it/~khanh/Preprints/12_K_SemDott0910_note.pdf Tran Vu Khan, University of Padua Seminar 2009/10]</ref>

Catlin was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Regularity of solutions of the <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann problem'' at the [[International Mathematical Congress|ICM]] in 1986 in Berkeley. In 1989 he received the inaugural [[Stefan Bergman Prize]].

His brother [[Paul Allen Catlin]] (1948–1995) also achieved fame as a mathematician, doing research on [[graph theory]].

==Selected publications==
*Necessary conditions for subellipticity of the <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann problem, [[Annals of Mathematics]], 117, 1983, 147–171 {{doi|10.2307/2006974}}
*Boundary invariants of pseudoconvex domains, Annals of Mathematics 120, 1984, 529–586 {{doi|10.2307/1971087}}
*Subelliptic estimates for the <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann problem on pseudoconvex domains, Annals of Mathematics, 126, 1987,  131–191 {{doi|10.2307/1971347}}
*Estimates of invariant metrics on pseudoconvex domains of dimension two, [[Mathematische Zeitschrift]] 200, 1989, 429–466 {{doi|10.1007/BF01215657}}
*as editor with Thomas Bloom, John P. D'Angelo, [[Yum-Tong Siu]]: [https://books.google.com/books/about/Modern_Methods_in_Complex_Analysis.html?id=KCoSRSC2En4C Modern methods in complex analysis], Annals of Mathematics Studies 137, Princeton University Press 1995 (dedicated to [[Robert Gunning (mathematician)|Robert Gunning]] and Joseph Kohn)
*with J. P. D'Angelo: [https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9511201 A stabilization theorem for Hermitian forms and applications to holomorphic mappings], [[arXiv]] preprint math/9511201, 1995
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=jSQECAAAQBAJ&pg=PA39 Global regularity of the <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann problem], in: ''Complex analysis of several variables'', Proc. Symp. Pure Math. Vol. 41, AMS, 1984, 39–49
*[https://books.google.com/books?id=OtzTCwAAQBAJ&oi=fnd&pg=PA93 Necessary conditions for subellipticity and hypoellipticity for the <math>\overline{\partial}</math>-Neumann problem on pseudoconvex domains], in: ''Recent Developments in Several Complex Variables'' ([[John Erik Fornæss|John E. Fornæss]], ed.), Annals of Mathematics Studies Vol. 100, 2016, 93–100.
